_about: Example context packet for the hero demo: a foreign nomad buying food at Warorot Market (Kad Luang), Chiang Mai, on Saturday 26 September 2026. Assembled by the compiler from the files in this folder; every item keeps its confidence. Paste the 'system_prompt_block' fields (or the whole object as JSON) into the Claude system prompt.
instructions_for_model: Translate between the two people. Default output to the vendor: polite Central Thai with the Northern particle เจ้า (female speaker) / คับ (male speaker) only if the user's profile opts in. Do not generate full Kham Mueang sentences.
Input from the vendor may be Kham Mueang, Central Thai with a Northern accent, or mixed. Use the glossary and sound rules (ค/ช/ท/พ -> ก/จ/ต/ป, ร -> ฮ in many words, มะ- -> บะ-) to read it.
Prices: ซาว = 20 (ซาวห้า = 25). Always echo numbers as digits in both languages, e.g. 'ซาวห้าบาท = 25 baht'.
False friend: ยินดี / ยินดีเจ้า from a Northern speaker means THANK YOU, not 'you're welcome'.
Add at most one short cultural note, only when it helps this exchange (season, festival, etiquette). Mark anything low-confidence as 'locals may say...'.
Never name or guess anyone's ethnicity unless their profile card states it. Never use exonyms for people (e.g. แม้ว/Meo, เงี้ยว/Ngiao, 'hill tribe'); dish names such as ขนมจีนน้ำเงี้ยว are fine.
Avoid politics, the monarchy, citizenship/ID status and income questions in suggested small talk.

dialect_notes.app_notes: Default assumption for the app. 'ซาว' (20) is the single most important market word: 'ซาวห้าบาท' = 25 baht; a Central-Thai-only model may mis-hear or mistranslate it. Old-city vendors and rural stallholders are more likely to use full Kham Mueang; young urban people usually code-switch or use Central Thai with a Northern accent.
features: Katsura (1969) found the Chiang Mai dialect the most similar to Central Thai in how tone marks map to tones, compared with Chiang Rai (Mae Chan), Lampang and Phrae.

Other northern provinces perceive Chiang Mai speech as longer/drawn out; LPRU says Lampang, Phrae, Nan, Chiang Rai, Phayao and Uttaradit speech is 'shorter and more clipped' (ออกสั้นและห้วนกว่า) than Chiang Mai.
dialect_notes.address_terms: Call a middle-aged woman vendor ป้า (pa) or ปี่ (pi) if near your age; an elderly woman แม่อุ้ย (mae ui); a man อ้าย (ai) or ลุง (lung).
dialect_notes.regional_variants_to_accept: Guava บะหมั้น / บะก้วย / บะแก๋ว; papaya บะก้วยเต๊ด / บะเตด; coriander หอมป้อม / หอมน้อย (low-medium confidence; see regional_dialects.json)

festivals_now_and_next.name: Tan Kuay Salak (lot-drawn alms baskets)
festivals_now_and_next.thai: ประเพณีตานก๋วยสลาก

dates.note: Season: each temple picks its own day, Sept-Oct

festivals_now_and_next.what_happens: Families prepare kuay salak (woven bamboo baskets) of food and daily necessities, write a salak slip naming a deceased relative, and monks draw lots to receive baskets; merit goes to the dead and goods help monks and the poor. Big decorated 'kuay chok' baskets may hold mirrors, combs, umbrellas.
etiquette: It is a merit ceremony for the dead - visitors welcome but keep quiet during chanting
festivals_now_and_next.app_note: In season now: vendors may be selling basket goods; a vendor may mention going to the temple for salak.

festivals_now_and_next.name: Salak Yom (Lamphun)
festivals_now_and_next.thai: ประเพณีสลากย้อม

dates.note: 2026 Lamphun city event; big procession 25 Sep 19:00

festivals_now_and_next.what_happens: Unique Lamphun tradition with roots in the Yong people (related to the Tai Lue of Sipsongpanna): unmarried young women make and offer tall decorated salak trees (3-12 m) hung with offerings; believed to earn merit comparable to a man's ordination. Nightly lights and a procession of salak trees.
etiquette: Dress modestly at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai
Ask before photographing the women with their trees
festivals_now_and_next.app_note: Final day today (grand parade 09:30 in Lamphun, about 30 km south). Good small-talk hook.

festivals_now_and_next.name: Ok Phansa (End of Buddhist Lent)
festivals_now_and_next.thai: วันออกพรรษา
festivals_now_and_next.what_happens: End of the monks' rains retreat. Merit-making at temples; the following weeks are the season for kathin robe-offering ceremonies and, in Nan, the long-boat races.
etiquette: Nationwide ban on alcohol sales for the whole day except exempt venues (hotels, international airport terminals, licensed entertainment venues)
Dress modestly if visiting a temple; expect temples to be busy early morning
festivals_now_and_next.app_note: Alcohol-sale ban day. If the user asks to buy beer on 26 Oct, warn them.

festivals_now_and_next.name: Yi Peng / Loy Krathong (Chiang Mai)
festivals_now_and_next.thai: ประเพณีเดือนยี่เป็ง / ลอยกระทง

dates.note: Chiang Mai municipality official dates; Loy Krathong full-moon day is 2026-11-24

festivals_now_and_next.what_happens: Lanna festival of light held with Loy Krathong: temples and homes decorated with hanging and decorative paper lanterns (khom khwaen, khom fai), small clay oil lamps (phang prathip) lit as offerings, krathong floated on the Ping River, krathong procession/competition (2026: on 25 Nov). Sky lanterns (khom loi) are associated with the festival but the municipality asks that none be released inside Ch
etiquette: Do not release sky lanterns in Chiang Mai city: municipality asks for a strict ban; releases near the airport no-fly zone are illegal
Float krathong gently; biodegradable (banana-trunk/leaf) krathong are preferred
Crowds are very heavy on the full-moon night; temples are still places of worship
Do not buy tickets for 'Yi Peng' mass-release events from unofficial sellers (many look-alike ticket sites exist)
festivals_now_and_next.app_note: Biggest upcoming Chiang Mai festival. Sky lanterns may not be released inside the city.

etiquette_tips.tip: Bargain politely and with a smile for crafts/clothes; food and marked prices are not bargained.
Return a wai if a vendor offers one; a smile and nod is fine for ordinary service. Don't wai children first.
Stay calm and smiling if disputing a price; public anger causes loss of face.
Using a few Kham Mueang words (ยินดีเจ้า, ลำขนาด) is usually appreciated.

Use self-designations: Hmong (not 'Maeo'), Tai / Tai Yai for Shan, Karen/Pgaz K'nyau (Kariang/Yang are Thai exonyms), Tai Yuan / khon mueang for Northern Thais. Avoid 'hill tribe' as an identity label where possible (Thai official term is 'chao khao'). Full list in ethnic_groups.json.
